Jordan — great to meet you and Alex today, appreciate the clear problem statement. Recap + next steps below. I attached the prompt set and a short schema examples file to get you started.

Recap (post-call):
- Use case: invoice data extraction -> JSON output (line items, totals, taxes) + small downstream categorical labels.
- Constraints: avg latency target 300–400ms p95, cost target ~ $0.005/token effective, schema compliance target >= 98%.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
- Model family: redwood-instruct-13b-rlhf for best balance of quality/latency for structured extraction.
- If you need lower cost at some quality tradeoff: redwood-quant-70b-int8 (with quantized path) — good throughput for batch jobs but higher p95 latency for single-shot calls.
- For strict schema enforcement: use our tool-calling + schema assertion layer (we validate model output against the JSON schema and can auto-retry up to N times with temperature/prompt adjustments).

Artifacts attached: prompt_set_v1.json (contains the extraction prompts we used), schema_examples.json (example expected outputs), benchmark_report_0618.pdf (summary of internal bench runs). Full results are in the Drive link below.

Proposed eval plan / next steps:
1) We’ll grant a 2-week eval workspace with sample tokens for Acme to run prompt_set_v1 against the two recommended model variants. (Marissa -> provisioning)
2) Acme runs the prompts and returns the eval results page (we’ll give a shared Drive and a simple scoring template).
3) We’ll run a parallel Redwood run and reconcile outputs, focusing on schema compliance, malformed output rate, and latency distribution.
4) If schema compliance <98%, we’ll test the auto-retry flow and report improvements.

Question for you: what is your tolerance for retries (max N) vs. additional latency? That will determine recommended retry policy.

Planned next meeting: 2026-06-27 10:00 AM PT to review initial pilot plan.

Thanks — attaching files now.

—

Perfect — thanks Alex/Rishi. Quick answers and what's attached/shared: 

1) Failure modes & our handling (high level):
   - Partial or truncated JSON: our validator flags as malformed. We run a single automatic correction attempt that re-invokes the model with an explicit "repair" prompt (low temperature, stronger constraints). If still malformed, we return an error code and optionally fall back to your deterministic parser.
   - Wrong types / extra keys: validator can coerce simple type mismatches (e.g., numbers in strings) when safe; for structural mismatches we try one repair pass.
   - Nested schema violations: treated same as malformed — we do up to N retries with progressively stricter prompts.

2) Retry policy recommendation (for pilot): max_retries=2, first retry uses repair prompt + temperature=0.0, second retry uses a short constrained generation with the schema embedded. That usually gets us from ~93–95% -> >=98% on structured tasks in our internal tests. Latency impact: expect p95 to increase by ~100–220ms when retries occur; we’ve found p95 stays <500ms for single-shot targets when retry rate <3%.

3) Attached + links: prompt_set_v1.json, schema_examples.json, eval_results_acme_q1.html, benchmark_report_0618.pdf, mutual_action_plan_acme.docx. Full raw run logs are in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-evals

4) HubSpot: HS-2026-4531 — Rishi confirmed $10k pilot credits; we can start provisioning as soon as Alex confirms the 2-retry tolerance.

Next steps (action items):
